tasks.title: No gate or config value is rewritten by the write scrub, and every redaction is journaled
tasks.description: PRIORITY (P122-R13). `_manifest_io.scrubbed_plan` runs `_machine_paths.scrubbed_values` over the WHOLE plan on every save (`atomic_write_json`, `save_plan_json`, `save_sharded`, `save_single_file`), so executable and config values are rewritten with everything else: a `meta.buildCommands` entry naming an interpreter under a home directory becomes the outside-repo token and the gate stops running, and with `--project-dir` below the checkout root an in-repo absolute path becomes checkout-relative while gate steps run with cwd=project. Invariant: an executable or config value is never silently rewritten - it is refused at the door that sets it, or exempt from the scrub. Do both: (1) exempt those fields from `scrubbed_plan` by their POSITION in the plan (`meta.buildCommands.*`, `meta.phaseGate`, `meta.fullGate`, each phase's `testGate`, each task's `tests.gate`, and any other field the plan executes - enumerate them from the readers of `_evidence_io.resolved_commands`), as a pointer table beside `scrubbed_plan`, never a key name at any depth (the flaw R11 removed from the ledger); (2) refuse a machine path in those fields at every door that writes them - audit-task's `--gate` on `add`, `scope`, `add-phase` and `retarget`, the panel settings save of `meta.buildCommands` through `_panel_write`, and derive-phase-gate's derived entry - each refusal naming the field and the remedy (a repo-relative or PATH-resolved spelling), with `tools/check-committed-pii.py` left as the backstop for a hand edit. (P122-R14) `scrubbed_values(keep=)` is a name-keyed exemption with no caller outside the mp8 case: replace it with the pointer exemption or delete it with mp8. (a) A finding whose `file` text names no resolvable path still yields a fix task with no files, which the plan gate then refuses edit by edit; refuse the add instead, naming each such finding and the `scope --files` remedy (or, from the drive, stop with that question) - never a task whose scope is empty by accident. (b) When a finding's resolution asks for a test, or the fix scope holds a test path, the fix task's gate includes the runner that test belongs to (through `_gate_derive`, the one place that maps a test path to its runner); when no runner can be derived, the note says why instead of leaving a lint/typecheck-only gate in silence. Regression: `--fixes` over a finding with `file: "(no path here)"` refuses naming it; a finding with `file: "src/a.ts"` and a resolution 'add a unit test' yields a gate holding the unit runner; the reported string `src/a.ts (x, y)` still scopes `src/a.ts` alone. Faults: F631.

tasks.title: A review-only offered gate entry never runs as a command; it reaches the reviewer, and scope can replace a task gate
tasks.description: (F635, reported from the testbed on 3.2.0) `meta.buildCommands.claimsMatchCode` held `review-only: sign-off reviewer refuses diff prose...`; the phase gate's `always` carried it, run-test-gate handed it to bash (exit 2, syntax error) and every task gate in the phase went red. `_gate_feed.OFFERED_GATES` offers `claimsMatchCode` as a read of the diff's prose - it has no command form - but gate derivation (`add --from-file` from meta.buildCommands, the phase gate's `always`) treats every key as a command. (1) An offered entry the catalog marks review-only (a `runs: false` field on the catalog entry), or any buildCommands value declaring itself `review-only:`, never enters a task or phase gate as a command: derivation skips it and says so, and the reviewer's brief carries its `asks` sentence as an instruction. (2) run-test-gate, handed such a step anyway (an older plan), records it as not a command - no shell run, no red gate - naming the remedy. (3) `audit-task scope` takes `--gate-set` and `--gate-drop` on a not-started task the way `retarget` takes them on a phase (a started task keeps its append-only rule, and the refusal names the exact spelling that is allowed). Regression: a plan with `claimsMatchCode: "review-only: ..."` derives a gate without it and the reviewer brief carries its sentence; run-test-gate given that step stays green and says not-a-command; scope --gate-set replaces a pending task's gate. Faults: F635.

tasks.title: A reused gate verdict is the newest measurement for its tree, and rerun never repeats a red a newer run superseded
tasks.description: (F636, reported from the testbed on 3.2.0) After the orchestrator recorded a green gate by hand (`run-test-gate --record`) and answered the drive's gate-red question with `rerun`, the drive sometimes printed GATE VERDICT REUSED and repeated its own OLDER red row for the same tree identity instead of the newer green row; three cycles passed before it took the green. Reuse selects the newest MEASURED row for the identity across every recorder, ordered by the one moment reader (`_evidence_io` ts order); a `rerun` answer never reuses a red row when a newer row exists for the same identity; and when a verdict is reused the banner names the row it repeats and, if a newer row for the identity exists, why that one was not taken. Regression: identity X holding an older drive red and a newer --record green -> `next --answer rerun` closes on the green (or measures afresh) and never prints the old red; identity X with only the old red still reuses it, banner naming it. Faults: F636.

tasks.title: sr23 waits for its child honestly, so the red-first helper's own suite is green inside a throwaway
tasks.description: (F637) test_stamp_verification's sr23 starts a nested `stamp-verification red` and waits at most a fixed short window for the child's `started` mark before sending SIGTERM; inside the red-first helper's own throwaway, under load, the child has not started when the signal lands, sr23 fails, HEAD's run of the suite is red, and every red-first over this suite is graded could-not-prove (P123.40 and P123.44 lost their proved red to it). Poll for the `started` mark against a deadline long enough for a loaded nested run; if the mark never appears, the case reports that it could not start the child (a could-not-run with its reason through the harness, not a FAIL of the removal it asserts); the removal assertion itself is unchanged. Regression: a child slowed past the old window still lets sr23 pass; a removal that leaves a throwaway worktree still fails it; the suite run inside `stamp-verification red`'s throwaway at HEAD is green. Also (F638): an executor that puts its new cases in a NEW stage and names `--stage <label>` after `--` is graded 'already red at HEAD', because at HEAD the label does not exist and the house runner fails on its unknown-stage check (P123.38, P123.44 and P123.45 all lost their proved red to this). When HEAD's run fails ONLY on that unknown-stage check, for a label the task's own test files introduce (absent at HEAD, present in the working tree), stamp-verification reads the baseline as 'the stage is new at HEAD' - green, the basis saying so - exactly as it reads a brand-new test file; any other HEAD failure keeps today's grading. Regression for this part: a task adding stage `zz` with one case red before the fix and green after proves; the same command where HEAD already has a red `zz` still grades already-red. Faults: F637, F638.

tasks.title: The newline lint reads this repository's own hooks too, and none of them writes text with a platform newline
tasks.description: Follow-up to the newline task, which emptied the pending list and extended `_output.text_write_newline_violations` to the plugin's hooks but left `.claude/hooks/` out of `NEWLINE_DIRS` because its files were outside that task's scope: arm-release-bypass.py, guard-release.py, guard-uncommitted.py and require-claim-block.py open text files for write with no newline. Give each write an explicit `newline="\n"` (or `newline=None` with a comment saying why the platform newline is wanted), add `.claude/hooks` to the lint's default walk when that directory exists, and keep the pending list empty. Regression: the lint flags a bare text-mode write in a `.claude/hooks`-shaped directory and reports nothing on the real tree.
